From some initial investigation, it does appear that the metrics module does require the javax.servlet.annotation package, though in using this annotation (i.e. WebListener), it is also using a deprecated Dropwizard class: com.codahale.metrics.servlets.AdminServletContextListener. Some cleanup here is certainly possible.
Can we isolate the Metrics-related cleanup or do they all hang together? I have reservations about the value of the Metrics-driven services anyway.
Yes, it seems possible to isolate the Metrics cleanup (i.e. javax.servlet.annotation) from the rest (i.e. javax.servlet.http)
Please re-open this ticket after merging the above PR.
Work to be continued on this ticket.
This ticket was based on the idea that the http-commons module was to be independent of JAX-RS, but I no longer see that as a realistic goal.
The fedora http modules rely on both javax.ws.rs.core and javax.servlet.http classes. It seems to make sense to consolidate these around javax.ws.rs.core
Also, the metrics module depends on a javax.servlet.annotation class. We should evaluate whether this is necessary.

At present, the maven configuration downgrades the servlet-api version to 3.0.1 (even though modeshape depends on 3.1.0). This causes some messiness for OSGi, and it would be good to straighten this out. (Removing the direct dependency may be the easiest approach)
